title: observability: token-level metrics + tracing dashboard and alert tuning for inference paths
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Adds a token-level metrics and tracing dashboard for inference request paths; refines alert thresholds for token latency and cost regressions. No user-facing API changes. Rollout: gradual enablement behind feature flag for 7 days, monitor cost and latency metrics.
description: Context: Customers and SRE teams have asked for higher-fidelity visibility into per-token cost and latency across the inference stack (frontend gateway -> router -> runtime). This PR adds token-level metrics ingestion, tracing spans, a Redwood Console dashboard, and tuned alerts to reduce false positives while surfacing real regressions. Motivation: recent incidents (SRE-214) showed regressions in batching/caching that only became visible at token granularity. Summary of changes: 1) metrics: emit per-request and per-token counters and histograms for token-generation latency and estimated token cost (new Prometheus labels: model, deployment, route, token_phase). 2) tracing: add spans around KV cache hits/misses and non-blocking batching boundaries; attach token-level annotations for large responses. 3) dashboards: new token-level dashboard with p50/p95/p99 token latency, token cost breakdown, KV cache hit rate, and routing fallbacks. 4) alerts: tuned alert rules to use 5m/15m windows and compare to historical baselines to reduce noise. Checklist: - [x] Metrics emitted from runtime and collector - [x] Tracing spans added with low overhead instrumentation - [x] Dashboard JSON + Console view config - [x] Alert rules with runbook links - [x] Backwards-compatible: labels are additive - [x] Load-tested (see commits) Deployment notes: feature-flagged rollout. Start with 5% of production traffic for Dedicated, monitor token_cost and token_latency_alerts for 48h, then 50% for 72h, then full. If alert rates increase >2x, rollback. Backfill: no schema changes to long-term metrics; retention unchanged. Testing: unit tests + integration tests against local tracing collector; load test simulating 10k concurrent connections with varied sequence lengths. Related: SRE-214, ENG-8421.

// services/runtime/metrics/collector.go - emit token histogram
metrics.TokenLatency.WithLabelValues(model, deployment, route, tokenPhase).Observe(latencyMs)

// services/runtime/tracing/instrumentation.go - add span
span := tracer.StartSpan(ctx, "kv-cache")
span.SetTag("kv.hit", hit)
span.Finish()

# observability/alerts/token_latency_cost_rules.yaml
- alert: TokenLatencyRegressed
  expr: increase(token_latency_bucket_sum[5m]) / increase(token_latency_count[5m]) > (avg_over_time(token_latency_p50[7d]) * 1.25)
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: /runbooks/token_latency

summary: Adds token-level observability (metrics + tracing), a Console dashboard, and tuned alerts to improve detection of inference regressions while controlling alert noise. Rollout is feature-flagged and monitored with a staged rollout plan.
impact_notes: Operational impact: small CPU/memory increase on runtime nodes when sampling disabled (~+1.8% CPU). Benefit: earlier detection of batching/cache regressions and clearer cost attributions per token. No user API changes.
follow_up: 1) Monitor token_cost and token_latency_alerts for 2 weeks post rollout and adjust sampling thresholds. 2) Add sapling to aggregate token cost into monthly billing exports (ENG-9002). 3) Consider promoting token-level traces to full trace links when end-to-end sampling detects anomalies.
notes_for_release_engineering: Feature-flag controlled. Enable at 5% for Dedicated, validate metrics and alert behavior for 48h, increase to 50% for 72h, then full. Runbook link: /runbooks/token_latency. No DB migrations required.
